reviews.question: Should the Indianapolis corridor registry be widened to cover ZIPs 46236 and 46239, admitting these three founder-approved identities?
reviews.why_this_is_not_a_census_question: This market holds every census row to exactly one registry corridor, and the corridor decides which neighbourhood PAGE a hotel is published on. Widening the registry is therefore a market-contract and publishing decision, not the census addition COVERAGE-001 authorised. Admitting these rows corridor-less would have broken the invariant; guessing a corridor would have published a hotel into a neighbourhood nobody chose.

evidence_today.identity_evidence: each page named its own address, and no census row holds any of the three addresses

options: extend an adjacent corridor (46236 sits beside keystone-castleton and east-i70; 46239 sits beside east-i70 and south)
declare a new corridor for the northeast/southeast doughnut
leave the registry as it is and keep these three out of the census
forbidden_until_ruled: admitting these three identities to the census
assigning any of them a corridor
editing the market contract corridor registry
reviews.default_if_never_ruled: the three stay out of the census and publish nothing

evidence: all three properties state their own city as Indianapolis on their own brand pages
the market contract enumerates its exclusions explicitly and neither ZIP is among them
both ZIPs are INTERIOR gaps, not an expansion: 46236 sits between declared 46256 and 46235; 46239 between declared 46229 and 46237
explicit corridor assignment is already how five census rows in ZIPs 46202/46222 are handled, and the boundary note documents the pattern
investigation_004.recommendation: EXPLICIT ASSIGNMENT of the three keys (46236 -> keystone-castleton, 46239 -> east-i70), which admits exactly these three and sweeps in no future hotel
